paper_sections.title: Damaged Insula Network Contributes to Depression in Parkinson’s Disease

description.value: The study examined resting-state insula functional connectivity in depressed Parkinson’s disease, non-depressed Parkinson’s disease, and normal control groups, and related connectivity differences to clinical scale scores.

design.value: Two groups of PD patients, with and without depression, and seventeen normal controls were recruited. Resting-state BOLD functional connectivity was compared among the groups using four anterior/posterior and left/right insula seed regions.

description.value: Scores were obtained from all subjects.

Hoehn and Yahr stage was reported for the two PD groups.
The PD diagnosis was made by a senior neurologist according to the UK PD Brain Bank criteria.

task_description.value: Subjects were instructed to relax with their eyes closed without falling asleep, and without directed systematic thought. This was confirmed after completion of scanning.

instructions.value: Relax with your eyes closed without falling asleep, and without directed systematic thought.

description.value: BOLD images were acquired using an echo planar imaging sequence with TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, flip angle = 90°, FOV = 240 × 240 mm², matrix = 64 × 64, slice thickness = 5 mm, slice gap = 1 mm, and 23 interleaved axial slices. A total of 185 resting-state BOLD images were acquired from each subject.

Anatomical images were acquired after functional imaging using a 3-D GRE T1-weighted sequence with TR/TE = 5.14 ms/1.17 ms, FOV = 240 × 240 mm², matrix = 256 × 256, slice thickness = 1.2 mm, no gap, and 124 sagittal slices.
A T2-weighted imaging sequence was also acquired.
A diffusion tensor imaging sequence was also acquired.
A susceptibility weighted imaging sequence was also acquired.

The first 10 images were excluded. Remaining images were slice-time corrected, realigned, regressed for Friston-24 head motion parameters and white matter and CSF signals using CompCor, normalized into standard space using DARTEL, resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm, smoothed with a 6-mm Gaussian kernel, detrended, and bandpass filtered at 0.01–0.1 Hz. Framewise displacement scrubbing excluded time points with FD > 0.5 mm; subjects with fewer than 130 remaining time points were excluded.

software.value: Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF), by YAN Chao-Gan, http://www.restfmri.net
Resting-State fMRI Data Analysis Toolkit (REST V1.8), http://www.restfmri.net

steps.value: The first 10 images were excluded from the analysis.
Slice timing was corrected using the middle slice as a reference.
Images were realigned to remove head motion.
Friston-24 head motion parameters and white matter and CSF signals calculated using the CompCor method were regressed out.
Images were normalized into standard space using DARTEL.
Images were resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxel size.
Images were smoothed using a 6-mm Gaussian kernel.
Bandpass filtering at 0.01–0.1 Hz was performed.
Subjects having head motion with >2 mm of translation or 2° of rotation were excluded.
Time points where FD > 0.5 mm were censored.
Subjects whose total length of data were <130 were excluded.

model_settings.value: Pearson’s correlation was calculated between the average time series within each insula ROI and other brain areas. The resulting connectivity maps were transformed to Z maps using Fisher r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Pearson’s correlation followed by Fisher r-to-z transformation

model_settings.value: Functional connectivity maps were compared among the three groups, with age and sex used as covariates. All PD subjects were pooled and compared with the NC group; depressed and non-depressed PD patients were then compared.
A one-sample t-test was used to demonstrate the connectivity patterns in each group.
Age and FD were compared among the three groups using one-way ANOVA.
Disease duration and scale scores were compared between the two PD groups using a two-sample t-test.
Signals from significant clusters were extracted to explore the relationship between insula connectivity and scale scores, controlling for age and sex.

estimator.value: partial correlation with age and sex controlled
